craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder at revealed authority. Sanskrit first: three predicates (thirteenfold, supreme, indicated) crowned by Śambhu himself → L4 sets predicates line 1, revealer line 2 (end-weight on the hand). Rows: row 1 (predicate-last — 'hand' lands last as svayam closes the verse). Rupture: em-dash after 'supreme' — the count breaks open into praise. Close: period on the revealer (authority rests). Minimal pass: 'Trika book' for 'Trika treatise' (singable, same doctrine); zero else. Read aloud: line 1 swells (thirteenfold, supreme, entire), dash breath, line 2 bows to the hand. Rejected: 'scriptures' for śāstreṣu — killed: book/treatise is the taught thing, scripture imports a canon-frame; naming the wonder ('how glorious') — killed: stating the suggested drops the dhvani-rank.

lines: Thirteenfold, supreme — the Śākta wisdom entire,
shown in every Trika book by Śambhu's own hand.
l4.sanskrit_cite: iti trayodaśavidhaṃ śāktaṃ vijñānamuttamam / sarveṣu trikaśāstreṣu sūcitaṃ śambhunā svayam

reads_against.argmap: The doctrine's authority is direct revelation, hence supreme.
c1_essence: Supreme wisdom revealed by Śambhu himself across every Trika treatise.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta with vīra-utsāha (wonder braced by resolve)
